For pneumonia: CURB-65 score, interpreted alongside clinical judgement. A score of 0 or 1 is low risk of death and suitable for home treatment — which is exactly why an admission on that score will be questioned.
For pneumonia: respiratory rate, oxygen saturation on room air, baseline saturation, and blood pressure — the saturation on room air is mandatory on admission as part of the discharge criteria.
For pneumonia: blood gases, plain radiology report, and serum urea?

no: Not covered, in all three protocols: sunglasses frames — dispensing one and swapping in medical lenses is recorded as FRAUD; tinted or coloured lenses; photochromic, polarised or transition lenses; ready-made reading glasses; and tinted cosmetic contact lenses even when they carry power.
Normal lenses must already include blue light reduction, UV protection, anti-reflective and scratch-resistant coatings at no extra cost.
Al Rajhi allows the patient to add uncovered extras on a cash basis; Tawuniya does not allow it even on cash.
